title: Adjoining a coherent inverse to an already invertible arrow preserves simplicial categories
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and their path-component categories $\pi_0$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], with the Bergner model structure whose weak equivalences are the Dwyer--Kan equivalences of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-cell-stability]. A cofibration has the left lifting property against all trivial fibrations, and trivial means also a weak equivalence. Let $A$ be the discrete simplicial category with objects $0,1$ and one nonidentity arrow $a:0\to1$. Let $\mathbb J$ be the discrete simplicial category with these two objects and exactly one arrow for each ordered pair, and let $i:A\to\mathbb J$ carry $a$ to its distinguished isomorphism. Choose any factorization $A\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}\mathbb J$ of $i$ with $j$ a cofibration and $q$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. For every small simplicial category $C$ and every simplicial functor $f:A\to C$ for which $[f(a)]$ is invertible in $\pi_0C$, the canonical map
$$C\longrightarrow C\amalg_A E$$
is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence and a cofibration. The pushout is the ordinary pushout of simplicial categories. No cofibration hypothesis on $f$, no local Kan hypothesis on $C$, and no requirement that $f(0)$ and $f(1)$ be distinct are imposed.

source.place: HTT Definition A.3.2.12, Remark A.3.2.14 (the reformulation with a cofibrant replacement), and Example A.3.2.18, printed pp. 862-863. Read online 2026-10-17. WANTED: archival HTT in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-category theorem.
